evidence: src/infrastructure/error-middleware.ts: errorMiddleware(err, _req, res, _next) is an Express error middleware, which is framework/transport logic and belongs in infrastructure

errorMiddleware maps ValidationError->400, NotFoundError->404, ConflictError->409 and everything else->500 using res.status(...).json(...). This translates errors into HTTP responses and makes no business decisions
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is an Express error-handling middleware that sits in the infrastructure layer. Its only job is transport: it maps domain error types to HTTP status codes and JSON response bodies. That is framework and transport logic, so it fits the infrastructure layer kind. It contains no business rules, no persistence and no application orchestration. Checking which domain error class an error belongs to and choosing a status code is HTTP adaptation, not a business decision.
